rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the later community as ʿĀd, the people of Hūd.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s reminder that ʿĀd succeeded Noah’s people and the order of prophetic stories in several sūras support the identification.
rows.anchor: ومجيء قصة هود على أثر قصة نوح في سورة الأعراف وسورة هود والشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī does not function like ilā as the complement of arsala; the people or village is instead the place of sending, as in Ruʾba’s verse and 25:51.
rows.anchor: ولكن الأمة أو القرية جعلت موضعا للإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explains arsala: through the messenger God told them to worship Him.
rows.anchor: أي : قلنا لهم على لسان الرسول : { اعبدوا الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without wāw, the accounts in al-Aʿrāf and Hūd answer an implied question; the wāw here connects their statement to the prior one, showing truth and falsehood together in stark contrast.
rows.anchor: على تقدير سؤال سائل قال : فما قال قومه ؟ فقيل له : قالوا كيت وكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting the Hereafter means meeting what it contains of reckoning, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: بلقاء ما فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب ، كقولك : يا حبذا جوار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun is omitted; the sense is “from your drink,” or the pronoun is understood from what precedes.
rows.anchor: حذف الضمير ، والمعنى : من مشروبكم ، أو حذف منه لدلالة ما قبله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā belongs to the conditional consequence and answers their opponents: they would lose their reason and be mistaken in their judgments.
rows.anchor: إذا } واقع في جزاء الشرط وجواب للذين قاولوهم من قومهم ، أي : تخسرون عقولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated innakum emphasizes the statement, made apt by the intervening time adverb; mukhrajūn may predicate the first innakum, or the second clause may be parsed as a nominal clause or conditional result.
rows.anchor: { إنكم } للتوكيد ، وحسن ذلك لفصل ما بين الأول والثاني بالظرف

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading omits the first innakum and reads “Does he promise you, when you have died…”.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( أيعدكم إذا متم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haihat is read with fatḥa, kasra, or ḍamma, with or without tanwīn, and with sukūn when pausing.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( هيهات ) بالفتح والكسر والضم ، كلها بتنوين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses the phrase as “distance from what you are promised” or “distance for what you are promised,” treating the tanuinated form as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قلت قال الزجاج في تفسيره : البعد لما توعدون ، أو بعد لما توعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām identifies what is remote after the exclamation, as in the clarifying lām in 12:23.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر : وهو أن يكون اللام لبيان المستبعد ما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hiyā is understood through the following explanation; the clause stands in place of “there is no life but our worldly life.”
rows.anchor: هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يعني به إلا بما يتلوه من بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative inna governs hiyā, which denotes life as a genus, giving the force of lā negating the whole genus.
rows.anchor: لأن ( إن ) النافية دخلت على ( هي ) التي في معنى الحياة الدالة على الجنس فنفتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean some people die while others are born: one generation passes away and another comes.
rows.anchor: أي يموت بعض ويولد بعض ، ينقرض قرن ويأتي قرن آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They accuse the messenger of inventing claims about his commissioning and resurrection after death, and say they will not believe him.
rows.anchor: ثم قالوا : ما هو إلا مفتر على الله فيما يدعيه من استنبائه له

none: The segment contains only the quoted verses, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jinnah here means madness.
rows.anchor: الجنة : الجنون وكانوا يعلمون أنه بريء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew the Prophet was sound in mind, but rejected him because his message opposed their desires and ingrained adherence to falsehood; unable to refute truth, they accused him of madness, sorcery, or poetry.
rows.anchor: ولكنه جاءهم بما خالف شهواتهم وأهواءهم ، ولم يوافق ما نشأوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some refrained from belief out of pride and fear of their people’s reproach for leaving their ancestors’ religion, not from hatred of truth; Abū Ṭālib is an example.
rows.anchor: قلت : كان فيهم من يترك الإيمان به أنفة واستنكافا من توبيخ قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī rejects the claim that Abū Ṭālib’s Islam was sound, arguing that Hamza’s and al-ʿAbbās’s Islam was known while his would not have remained hidden.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : بزعم بعض الناس أن أبا طلب صح إسلامه . قلت : يا سبحان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and their inhabitants stand by truth; if truth followed their desires and became falsehood, the world would lose its foundation and order.
rows.anchor: دل بهذا على عظم شأن الحق ، وأن السماوات والأرض ما قامت ولا من فيهن إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the truth is Islam brought by Muḥammad; if it turned into their shirk, God would bring the Resurrection and destroy the world without delay.
rows.anchor: أو أراد أن الحق الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says al-ḥaqq means God.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : أن الحق هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God followed their desires and commanded shirk and sins, He would be a Satan rather than God and could not uphold the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : لو كان الله إلاها يتبع أهواءهم ويأمر بالشرك والمعاصي ، لما كان إلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-dhikrhim can mean the Book that is their reminder, admonition, legacy, or source of pride.
rows.anchor: { بذكرهم } أي بالكتاب الذي هو ذكرهم ، أي : وعظهم أو وصيتهم وفخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the reminder they had wished for, saying that if they possessed one from earlier peoples they would be sincere servants of God.
rows.anchor: أو بالذكر الذي كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون : لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading is bi-dhikrāhum.
rows.anchor: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين . وقرىء : ( بذكراهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include kharājan fa-kharāj, kharjan fa-kharj, and kharjan fa-kharāj.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( خراجا فخراج ) و ( خرجا فخرج ) ( خرجا فخراج )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj or kharāj can denote land dues paid to the ruler or a worker’s wages or stipend.
rows.anchor: وهو ما تخرجه إلى الإمام من زكاة أرضك . وإلى كل عامل من أجرته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One distinction is that kharj is voluntary giving, while kharāj is an obligatory payment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخرج : ما تبرعت به . والخراج : ما لزمك أداؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers kharj as narrower and kharāj as broader, since added wording adds meaning; this favors kharjan fa-kharāj.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن الخرج أخص من الخراج ، كقولك : خراج القرية ، وخرج الكردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: do you ask them for a small human payment for guiding them, when the greater gift from the Creator is better?
rows.anchor: يعني : أم تسألهم على هدايتك لهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق ، فالكثير من عطاء الخالق خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghalabat ʿalaynā means it mastered and possessed them, as when someone takes something from another and owns it.
rows.anchor: {غلبت علينا } ملكتنا ، من قولك : غلبني فلان على كذا ، إذا أخذه منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wretchedness is the evil end God knew they deserved because of their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: والشقاوة سوء العاقبة التي علم الله أنهم يستحقونها بسوء أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read shaqwatunā or shaqāwatunā, with either fatḥa or kasra on the shīn.
rows.anchor: قرىء : { شقوتنا } وشقاوتنا بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhsāʾū fīhā means be humiliated and driven off like rebuked dogs; Arabic says a dog was driven off or drove itself off.
rows.anchor: { اخسئوا فيها } ذلوا فيها وانزجروا كما تنزجر الكلاب إذا زجرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means not to speak about lifting the punishment, since it will neither be lifted nor lightened.
rows.anchor: { ولا تكلمون } في رفع العذاب ، فإنه لا يرفع ولا يخفف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes this their last speech; afterward they only sigh, pant, and howl like dogs, no longer understanding or being understood.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو آخر كلام يتكلمون به ، ثم لا كلام بعد ذلك إلا الشهيق والزفير والعواء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they make six appeals, each for a thousand years, answered by refusal or rebuke; the cited sequence includes 32:12, 40:11–12, 43:77, 14:44, 35:37, and 23:99,108.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : إن لهم ست دعوات : إذا دخلوا النار قالوا : ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats the reminder of God’s favor in not hastening punishment and omits the conditional answer as earlier; repeating the omission intensifies emphasis, as with al-Tawwāb, al-Raʾūf, and al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: وكرر المنة بترك المعاجلة بالعقاب ، حاذفا جواب لولا كما حذفه ثمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī buyūtin may attach to the preceding description: the niche lamp is in some of God’s houses, namely mosques.
rows.anchor: {فى بيوت } يتعلق بما قبله . أي : كمشكاة في بعض بيوت الله وهي المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead attach to yusabbiḥu, meaning men glorify God in houses; the repeated location is like saying someone is in the house sitting in it.
rows.anchor: أو بما بعده ، وهو يسبح ، أي : يسبح له رجال في بيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing supplies an omitted verb, “glorify in houses,” as in the cited construction from 27:12.
rows.anchor: أو بمحذوف كقوله : { وأدخل يدك فى } ( النمل : 27 ) أي سبحوا في بيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s permission means His command, and raising the houses means building them, as in 79:28 and 2:127.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإذن : الأمر . ورفعها : بناؤها ، كقوله :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are mosques that God commanded to be built.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي المساجد ، أمر الله أن تبنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also allows “raised” to mean that the mosques are honored and elevated in rank.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي المساجد ، أمر الله أن تبنى ، أو تعظيمها والرفع من قدرها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command is not to raise the buildings but to honor them; the following mention of God’s name suits this reading.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله عنه : ما أمر الله أن ترفع بالبناء ، ولكن بالتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God’s name in the houses applies generally to every kind of remembrance.
rows.anchor: { ويذكر فيها اسمه } أوفق له ، وهو عام في كل ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās specifies that God’s name is mentioned by reciting His Book there.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : وأن يتلى فيها كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusabbaḥu is also read passively and can attach to one of the adverbials; rijāl is nominative through the implied active yusabbiḥu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يسبح ) على البناء للمفعول ، ويسند إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading tasabbaḥu has kasra on the bāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar reads tāʾ with fatḥa, making morning and evening times the subject, with their Lord intended.
rows.anchor: وتسبح ، بالتاء وكسر الباء . وعن أبي جعفر رضي الله عنه بالتاء وفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, meaning evening; bil-ghuduww means mornings.
rows.anchor: والآصال : جمع أصل وهو العشي . والمعنى : بأوقات الغدو ، أي : بالغدوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is wa-l-īṣāl, entering into evening; āṣala follows the patterns of aẓhara and aʿtama.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( والإيصال ) وهو الدخول في الأصيل . يقال : آصل ، كأظهر وأعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tijāra is the trader’s craft of buying and selling for profit; sale is singled out because a profitable sale is the trader’s sure objective and distracts more than a purchase whose gain is only expected later.
rows.anchor: التجارة : صناعة التاجر ، وهو الذي يبيع ويشتري للربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade may name buying as well as selling, using the general term for one type; another view limits it to caravan commerce and importing goods.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يسمى الشراء تجارة ، إطلاقا لاسم الجنس على النوع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation restricts tijāra to caravan merchants; itʿajara means to bring goods in.
rows.anchor: وقيل : التجارة لأهل الجلب ، اتجر فلان في كذا : إذا جلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in iqāma compensates for the root ʿayn dropped by defective morphology; the original is iqwām, and the construct form drops the compensating letter because the genitive relation takes its place, as in the cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: التاء في إقامة ، عوض من العين الساقطة للإعلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts and eyes may physically turn in terror and panic, as in 33:10; alternatively their conditions change, so sealed hearts understand and blind eyes see.
rows.anchor: وتقلب القلوب والأبصار : إما أن تتقلب وتتغير في أنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan mā ʿamilū means the best reward for their deeds, as in 10:26.
rows.anchor: { أحسن ما عملوا } أي أحسن جزاء أعمالهم ، كقوله : { للذين أحسنوا الحسنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They glorify and fear God so that He multiplies their reward and adds further grace; al-ḥusnā wa-ziyāda likewise means reward plus an increase beyond it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى يسبحون ويخافون ، ليجزيهم ثوابهم مضاعفا ويزيدهم على الثواب تفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gift without reckoning is grace; reward is measured according to what is deserved, and divine gifts may be grace, recompense, or compensation.
rows.anchor: وعطاء الله تعالى : إما تفضل وإما ثواب ، وإما عوض { والله يرزق } ما يتفضل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address consoles the Prophet and promises victory: every earlier prophet faced his people’s enmity, and God guides and helps him to overcome them.
rows.anchor: ثم أقبل عليه مسليا ومواسيا وواعدا النصرة عليهم ، فقال : { وكذالك } كان كل نبي قبلك مبتلى بعداوة قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They made the Qurʾān abandoned by leaving it and turning away from both it and belief in it.
rows.anchor: ناصرا لك عليهم مهجورا : تركوه وصدوا عنه وعن الإيمان به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says someone who learns and teaches the Qurʾān but neglects a hanging muṣḥaf will face it on Judgment Day as it asks God to judge between them for being abandoned; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 773 ) ( من تعلم القرآن وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, from hajara meaning to rave, they called the Qurʾān nonsense, falsehood, and tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من هجر ، إذا هذي ، أي : جعلوه مهجورا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second alternative is that they abandoned it by making noise when it was recited, as in 41:26.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنهم كانوا إذا سمعوه هجروا فيه ، كقوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahjūr can mean hijr, an action noun like majlūd or maʿqūl; the phrase then means they made the Qurʾān nonsense or an object of abandonment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المهجور بمعنى الهجر ، كالمجلود والمعقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿaduww may be singular or plural, as in 26:77.
rows.anchor: والعدو : يجوز أن يكون واحدا وجمعا . كقوله : { فإنهم عدو لى }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the speaker in this statement is the Messenger on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى : وقال الرسول يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzzila here means anzala; otherwise the wording would be strained.
rows.anchor: { نزل } ههنا بمعنى أنزل لا غير ، كخبر بمعنى أخبر

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand for one-piece revelation is an objection showing their flight from truth and refusal to follow it.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا من اعتراضاتهم واقتراحاتهم الدالة على شرادهم عن الحق وتجافيهم عن اتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī identifies the objectors as Quraysh.
rows.anchor: والقائلون : قريش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification says the objectors were Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask why the Qurʾān was not sent down at once, like the three earlier scriptures, instead of in portions.
rows.anchor: قالوا : هلا أنزل عليه دفعة واحدة في وقت واحد كما أنزلت الكتب الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection is pointless because the Qurʾān’s inimitability and force as proof do not differ whether it came all at once or in parts.
rows.anchor: وهذا فضول من القول ومماراة بما لا طائل تحته ؛ لأن أمر الإعجاز والاحتجاج به لا يختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that it was sent down in portions; gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet’s heart so he can comprehend and memorize it piece by piece.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { كذالك } جواب لهم ، أي : كذلك أنزل مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet needed gradual reception because, unlike Moses, David, and Jesus, he was unlettered and could not read or write.
rows.anchor: والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فارقت حاله حال موسى وداود وعيسى عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān was revealed gradually over twenty years; another report gives twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: فأنزل عليه منجما في عشرين سنة . وقيل : في ثلاث وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation also matched events and answers to questioners, and allowed abrogating and abrogated passages, which requires piecemeal revelation.
rows.anchor: وأيضا : فكان ينزل على حسب الحوادث وجوابات السائلين ، ولأن بعضه منسوخ وبعضه ناسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although dhālika appears to point back to the demand for one-piece revelation, that demand implies asking why it was not revealed in parts, so the answer means it was.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : ذلك في كذلك يجب أن يكون إشارة إلى شيء تقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to produce even one short sūra, followed by resort to confrontation and war, exposes their failed challenge; asking for the whole assumes they could meet it in parts.
rows.anchor: والدليل على فساد هذا الاعتراض : أنهم عجزوا عن أن يأتوا بنجم واحد من نجومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rattalnāhu may coordinate with the verb governing dhālika, so the sense is that God divided and ordered the revelation.
rows.anchor: ورتلناه } معطوف على الفعل الذي تعلق به كذلك ، كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means God commanded measured recitation, as in 73:4.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : وأمرنا بترتيل قراءته ، وذلك قوله :

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: A report attributed in the preceding passage to ʿĀʾisha describes the Prophet’s measured recitation: unlike rapid reading, a listener could count its letters; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ( 774 ) ( لا كسردكم هذا ، لو أراد السامع أن يعد حروفه يعدها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root image of tartīl is the even spacing of teeth, whose whiteness is likened to chamomile.
rows.anchor: وأصله : الترتيل في الأسنان : وهو تفليجها . يقال : ثغر رتل ومرتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that revelation was spaced out over twenty years rather than delivered in closely spaced installments.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو أن نزله مع كونه متفرقا على تمكث وتمهل في مدة متباعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever they raise a bizarre, invalid question, God provides a true answer with a better meaning and outcome.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتونك } بسؤال عجيب من سؤالاتهم الباطلة كأنه مثل في البطلان إلا أتيناك نحن بالجواب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the example is an extraordinary condition they demand for the Prophet, such as an angel companion, treasure, garden, or one-piece revelation; God gives the fitting sign and clearest proof according to His wisdom.
rows.anchor: أو لا يأتونك بحال وصفه عجيبة يقولون : هلا كانت هذه صفتك وحالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piecemeal revelation with a challenge to match even a portion makes a clearer proof of inimitability than a challenge to match the complete book at once.
rows.anchor: يعني : أن تنزيله مفرقا وتحديهم بأن يأتوا ببعض تلك التفاريق كما نزل شيء منها : أدخل في الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage exposes their contempt for the Prophet’s path and rank: people dragged on their faces to Hell would see their place as worse and their way as more astray if fair.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل لهم : إن حاملكم على هذه السؤالات أنكم تضللون سبيله وتحتقرون مكانه ومنزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makānan may mean honor and rank, or a dwelling and abode, as in 19:73.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالمكان : الشرف والمنزلة ، وأن يراد الدار والمسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a path astray is a figurative attribution of misguidance.
rows.anchor: ووصف السبيل بالضلال من الإسناد المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you not seen” means consider the work and power of your Lord.
rows.anchor: ألم تر إلى ربك } ألم تنظر إلى صنع ربك وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extending shade means making it spread out so people can benefit from it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مد الظل : أن جعله يمتد وينبسط فينتفع به الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had willed, shade would remain fixed at the base of each mountain, building, or tree, without spreading and therefore useless to anyone.
rows.anchor: أي لاصقا بأصل كل مظل من جبل وبناء وشجرة . غير منبسط فلم ينتفع به أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade’s spreading is described as motion and its remaining fixed as stillness.
rows.anchor: سمي انبساط الظل وامتداده تحركا منه وعدم ذلك سكونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People infer shade’s location, movement, expansion, and contraction from the sun’s course, and plan when to use or avoid shade accordingly.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كون الشمس دليلا : أن الناس يستدلون بالشمس وبأحوالها في مسيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s taking the shade back means erasing it through the sun’s brightness.
rows.anchor: وقبضه إليه : أنه ينسخه بضح الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shade is withdrawn gradually; this slow process has many benefits, while instant withdrawal would disrupt people’s use of sun and shade.
rows.anchor: يسيرا } أي على مهل . وفي هذا القبض اليسير شيئا بعد شيء من المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks increasing magnitude: the second stage exceeds the first and the third exceeds both, like events separated by greater intervals in time.
rows.anchor: موقعها لبيان تفاضل الأمور الثلاثة : كان الثاني أعظم من الأول ، والثالث أعظم منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account begins with shade cast by the sky over the spread earth before a luminary existed; God could have left it fixed, but then created the sun over it.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر : وهو أنه مد الظل حين بنى السماء كالقبة المضروبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account, the sun is a guide over shade like a guide on a road; the shade lengthens, shortens, expands, and contracts with it.
rows.anchor: ونصبها دليلا متبوعا له كما يتبع الدليل في الطريق ، فهو يزيد بها وينقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taking of shade may refer to its removal at the Resurrection by removing the celestial bodies and other causes that cast it; “to Us” and “gently” support this reading.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد : قبضه عند قيام الساعة بقبض أسبابه وهي الأجرام التي تلقي الظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is compared with God’s description of the gathering as easy in 50:44.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { ذلك حشر علينا يسير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night’s darkness is compared to a covering garment because it conceals.
rows.anchor: شبه ما يستر من ظلام الليل باللباس الساتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subāt means death; one asleep is called masbūt because life is cut off, as in 6:60.
rows.anchor: والسبات : الموت . والمسبوت : الميت ؛ لأنه مقطوع الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects taking subāt to mean rest because the parallel nushūr, awakening or resurrection, rules it out.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : هلا فسرته بالراحة ؟ قلت : النشور في مقابلته يأباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse demonstrates the Creator’s power and bounty: the night’s concealment has many religious and worldly benefits.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمته على خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep and wakefulness resemble death and life and provide a lesson to anyone who reflects.
rows.anchor: والنوم واليقظة وشبههما بالموت والحياة ، أي عبرة فيها لمن اعتبر

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqmān tells his son that, just as one sleeps and is awakened, one dies and is raised again.
rows.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه : يا بني ، كما تنام فتوقظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham knew they worshipped idols; he asked to show these objects did not deserve worship, like asking a trader about his property before pointing out that slaves are not property.
rows.anchor: كان إبراهيم عليه السلام يعلم أنهم عبدة أصنام ؛ ولكنه سألهم ليريهم أن ما يعبدونه ليس من استحقاق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the question asks only what they worship, they answer with their whole story and proudly add that they remain devoted to idols, displaying their feelings too.
rows.anchor: قلت : هؤلاء قد جاءوا بقصة أمرهم كاملة كالمبتهجين بها والمفتخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elaborate answer resembles asking a swaggering person what he wears and hearing that he wears a fine robe and drags its train among neighborhood women.
rows.anchor: ومثاله أن تقول لبعض الشطار : ما تلبس في بلادك ؟ فيقول : ألبس البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say “we remain devoted” because they worshipped the idols during the day, not at night.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا : نظل ، لأنهم كانوا يعبدونها بالنهار دون الليل
